cut: v1 (12 Nov, en only). Pitch B of plan/PITCHES-11-11.md. Device: a BORROWED FORMAT in one unbroken shot. The car's sat-nav tells the story from the dashboard: it announces the closure, lists who is flying, and recalculates. Every fact is on the sat-nav's own screen.
argument: For a week in November a stretch of Highway 9 near Kuopio closes so the Air Force can land Hornets on it; allied jets fly too, and Finland's new F-35s sit it out.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

text.en: In 300 meters, / give way to / [fighter jets].

captions.source: The sat-nav's own idiom; the satire's line, not a quoted notice. What it stands on: the Highway 9 traffic notice for the Jännevirta road base near Kuopio/Rissala, 18–25 Nov 2026, during the Air Force exercise Protective Fence 26 (Nordic Defence Sector; Siilinjärvi municipality's notice; search summaries, 9–12 Nov). '300 meters' is the sat-nav phrase, not a measured distance.

text.en: Road closed. / The Air Force / is [landing here].

captions.source: Finnish Air Force, 'Protective Fence 26 to be the Finnish Air Force's main exercise of the year' (ilmavoimat.fi): 19–27 Nov 2026, over 40 aircraft including 20 F/A-18 Hornets, about 4,100 people, dispersed operations from bases, civilian airports and a highway strip. Verkkouutiset repeats the figures. The highway landings are claimed for Finnish Hornets only. Search summaries, 11–12 Nov; the Air Force's page could not be opened from the build machine.

Dutch F-35As at Rissala (the Air Force's own page, per search summary 12 Nov); French Rafales from Rovaniemi and Swedish Gripens from Kallax (Nordic Defence Sector; AeroTime). 'Flying', not 'landing': no source puts allied jets on the highway strip.

AeroTime: Finland's own F-35As do not take part; the first two reached Rovaniemi on 18 Sep 2026. One trade source plus one unattributed summary (12 Nov). 'Finland's' stays in the line because Dutch F-35s do take part. To confirm on the Air Force's page before posting.
The turn: the satire's own line in the sat-nav's voice. Not a factual claim beyond the documented closure for the road base.

props: In-world text stays in its own language: the road block's sign reads TIE SULJETTU / ROAD CLOSED, and the roadside post carries a speed limit and the red Highway 9 plate. The sat-nav is an invented generic device with no brand; its clock and map are props. The jet is a simplified twin-tail fighter in plain grey with no markings. No people, no faces. The landing over a stopped car is a picture of the joke, not a depiction of how the road base operates: the real closure keeps traffic away from the strip.

post.en: In 300 meters, give way to fighter jets. Highway 9 at Jännevirta near Kuopio is closed 18–25 Nov: the Air Force lands Hornets on it in Protective Fence 26 (19–27 Nov, 40+ aircraft). Dutch, French and Swedish jets fly too. Finland's new F-35s sit it out.
